risks.note: Exposes Sagility to U.S. regulatory, economic and outsourcing-related developments - healthcare policy shifts, proposed measures such as the HIRE Act and state-level anti-outsourcing bills. Mitigations cited: deepening presence across both payer and provider segments, expanding into adjacent higher-value areas such as clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, regulatory-compliance and information-security focus, a multi-country delivery footprint (U.S., Jamaica, Colombia onshore/nearshore; India and the Philippines offshore) and negligible dependency on H1B visas.
risks.risk: Total dependence on a single end-market: the entire revenue base comes from the U.S. healthcare industry, with exports contributing 100% of turnover

risks.note: Consolidation, mergers, acquisitions or restructuring among healthcare payers and providers may cause vendor rationalization, contract renegotiation, volume reallocation or pricing pressure. Mitigations: diversifying across payer and provider segments, scaling end-to-end RCM in providers, higher-value clinical/patient-support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy, multi-year performance-linked contracts, the BroadPath-led entry into mid- and small-market accounts, and proactive engagement during client M&A.
risks.risk: Client concentration and client restructuring - the top 10 client groups contribute 83.9% of total revenue

risks.note: Revenues are linked to client-driven transaction volumes that can swing with membership trends, cost pressures, regulatory change, outsourcing decisions or client reprioritisation, affecting revenue predictability, capacity utilization and operating leverage. Mitigated through diversified revenue streams, flexible operating models, multi-year and outcome-based constructs, dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent and multi-geo scalable delivery, plus platform integration that raises client dependence and reduces insourcing likelihood.
risks.risk: Fluctuation in client business volumes, including the risk of clients insourcing work

risks.note: Competition combined with client cost-efficiency focus drives evolving commercial constructs and pricing dynamics. Sagility responds with an integrated domain-led operating model, a shift to outcome-based and managed-services constructs (value-led rather than price-led), non-linear output-based commercial models, expansion into higher-value clinical and adjacent lines, geo-shifts/multi-shore cost optimisation, and regular monitoring of account margins with periodic reporting to leadership.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure from global outsourcing providers, broad-based IT/business services firms, specialised healthcare-focused companies and clients' own in-house/digital capabilities

risks.note: Data breaches or non-compliance with stringent U.S. and global data-protection regimes (HIPAA, HITECH, CCPA, GDPR) could trigger regulatory action, financial penalties, lost business and reputational damage; delayed incident reporting is itself a compliance exposure. Controls include encryption, identity management, access controls and network protection, periodic risk assessments, vulnerability testing and independent external reviews, privacy impact assessments, data mapping, third-party data-sharing controls, a defined incident-management process owned by Compliance and Cybersecurity, training and awareness, and market-benchmarked cyber insurance.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy - handling sensitive protected health information across a partly remote workforce

risks.note: Elevated attrition and wage inflation affect service continuity, cost structures and margin profile; permanent-employee voluntary attrition (above 90 days) was 29.4% in FY 2026 versus 27.5% in FY 2025. Loss of senior leaders who hold deep domain expertise and long-standing client relationships could impair client confidence and service continuity. Mitigated through competitive, market-aligned compensation and benefits programmes.
risks.risk: Talent management, attrition and wage inflation in a competitive talent market, including key-management succession

risks.note: Frequent regulatory change increases compliance complexity and multi-jurisdiction operations increase legal exposure; non-compliance may result in penalties, financial strain and reputational damage. Managed through periodic Legal-team oversight, regular compliance status reporting (including exceptions) to Senior Management, the Audit Committee and the Board, and refreshing compliance frameworks as regulations evolve.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance complexity from operating across multiple geographies

risks.note: Unethical practices may invite regulatory scrutiny and penalties, and misconduct can damage brand reputation and stakeholder trust, potentially reducing investor confidence and access to financing. Addressed through a formal whistleblower mechanism allowing confidential reporting, with matters reviewed under established protocols and the code of conduct.
